HF diet-induced obesity in rats increases blood pressure and decreases the responsiveness to mu-opioid agonists.

the effects of high fat-induced obesity on cardiovascular and physical activity as related to opioid responsiveness.
the effect of HF diet-induced obesity on the cardiovascular system and physical activity.
the effects of high fat-induced obesity on blood pressures and physical activity as related to mu opioid receptors.

HF-induced obesity does increase blood pressure, but does not alter the cardiovascular responsiveness to the mu opioid system.
HF-induced obesity did not affect the mu opioid responsiveness in the CNS.
HF diet induced obesity is associated with a higher SBP and increased heart rate in conscious unanesthetised rats.

obesity and hypertension are associated with an increased responsiveness to mu opioids, which is not the case for HF-induced obesity.
